Summarize the following text in one sentence.

Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae and some bacteria turn light into chemical energy. In the chloroplasts, chlorophyll absorbs mostly red and blue light. That energy splits water molecules, releasing oxygen as a by-product, and drives the production of ATP and NADPH. In the Calvin cycle these carriers power the fixation of carbon dioxide from the air into three-carbon sugars, which the plant then builds into glucose, starch and cellulose. Nearly all the oxygen in the atmosphere and most of the energy in food chains come from this process, and its rate depends on light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, temperature and the supply of water.
